questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I looked for an area that was different both in nature and culture. It was important to experience something new that could help develop me as a person, and I generally believe that going to a different country - no matter where - would help me reach this goal.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would recommend everyone to go - as long as you know that it takes time, money and isn't 'just' a vacation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, I felt very prepared - but at the same time overwhelmed with information before I left to a point that I was stressed that I wouldn't have time to do it all or maybe even forget something. But it turned out to be simple once I got there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were given thorough email and talks upon arrival with detailed plans of where to go and what to do first. Otherwise you could write and email and ask og just talk to another exchange student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through ETH, so sign up for housing. Use woko

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice because you get to see the city, otherwise I would not move around at all

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with being offered housing and living with other exchange student, but the living situation was quite weird and at times stressful since we were 170 students sharing 1 kitchen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you are send forward from KU they will send you and email and ask you to apply in english. Then you et accepted and have to fill out an mobility online form but ETH version. Here they give you everything you need to know.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emailing the exchange coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, not the same classes were available, some were not at all what they were made out to be on the description, some were cancelled. All in all I ended up with completely different classes (that I was very happy about)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of how time consuming studying at ETH is. If you want time to explore exchange life then maybe this isn't the host institution for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high level, but I was able to follow, but it takes work. High workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Style of teaching in my case was almost no exercises and almost only lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Climate Change
International Environmental Politics
Resource and environmental economics
Ecosystem conservation and restoration
An introduction to sustainability in the built environment
Cooperation and Conflict over International Water Resources
Seminar in Glaciology
Acroecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend:
- cooperation and conflict over international resources
because it's a nice match between hydrology and politics and very scientifically based
Ecosystem conservation and restoration was also amazing and a great opportunity to interact through exercises with leading scientists in biodiversity

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything in switzerland is expensive - nothing was surprising, but food and transport budget need to be high.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Free sports at uni

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great opportunities to play free sports

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free sports, bars, trips with departments, erasmus network events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to erasmus events or events at your student deparment - it really pays off in the end.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the opera house in zurich and get the student tickets 1,5 hour before a play starts. Or go to the seabed enge and jump in the lake and enjoy sauna afterwards.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You need to ask first and make conversation - cause they are very friendly, but maybe a bit closed.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's very like danish culture in many ways

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the high workload at ETH
Be aware of the high living costs of Switzerland
Make sure to go hiking in the Alps a lot! It's amazing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first two weeks of the semester you get to try out which courses you like, so you don't need to decide 100% before you go there

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting that many people and being that independent

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not seeing my boyfriend and FOMO from other exchange student - "am I experiencing enough?"

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
